Subject: Clarify IP + training use in Order Form before exec review

Hi Monica —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to lock down a couple of items before our CFO signs the Order Form: specifically, (1) who owns generated outputs (search results, summaries, patient-facing content), and (2) whether Redwood can use CypherHealth data or outputs to improve or retrain models.

Our preference is that CypherHealth retains title to all outputs and that Redwood may not train models on any customer-provided content without explicit, per-deal consent. We can consider a narrow feedback mechanism (quality improvements, bug fixes) but want to avoid broad training licenses.

Can you share Redwood's standard Order Form language and a short summary of what you need to operate (logs, examples, anonymized telemetry)? We need this by EOD Tuesday to keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Data Products
CypherHealth

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I'm looping in Aditya (legal) and Rishi (commercial) to propose language that balances your requirement to retain outputs with Redwood's need to operate and improve the service.

Quick summary of what Redwood typically requires operationally:
- Short-term request / error logs (retained for 30 days by default) for debugging and incident response.
- Aggregated telemetry (latency, token counts, feature flags) for performance and billing reconciliation.
- Optional anonymized feedback snapshots when customers opt-in for quality tuning. These are never tied back to PII in our standard flows.

We're preparing a suggested redline for the Order Form and a concise feedback license that limits training to aggregated, de-identified data, and includes an opt-out for customers who do not want any feedback use.

I'll send the redline in the next message; if procurement needs a sign-off path, suggest a 48-hour legal review SLA so we don't slip the OPO sign date.

—Monica
Account Director, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed redlines + rationale (Order Form / Feedback License)

Folks —

Draft redlines attached (CYH_Proposed_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx) and copied below as plain text for quick review. I tried to minimize commercial risk while respecting CypherHealth's commercial position. Key points:

1) Outputs: Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated by the Service ("Customer Outputs"); Redwood receives only a limited, non-exclusive right to display or transmit Customer Outputs to provide the Service (e.g., cache for latency). We explicitly exclude any assignment or transfer of title.

2) Feedback / Training: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified Customer Feedback ("Feedback Data") to improve service quality (bug fixes, model evaluation) but may not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train new base models or large-scale model retraining without explicit, opt-in written consent.

3) Opt-out: Customer can opt-out of Feedback Data collection for training via the Order Form checkbox. If opted-out, Redwood will still process requests to provide the service but will not store long-term examples for model improvement.

4) Safety & Anonymization: Feedback Data used for improvement must be subject to our standard anonymization pipeline and cannot contain PHI as provided by the customer; if PHI is in scope, we will only retain logs for incident response and troubleshooting and will not use it for training.

Proposed plain-text clause (please review and flag any operational blockers):

"Customer Outputs. Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to outputs produced by the Service that are the direct result of Customer inputs (\"Customer Outputs\"). Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to copy, cache and display Customer Outputs solely to deliver the Service to Customer and fulfill its obligations under this Agreement. Under no circumstances will Customer be deemed to have transferred ownership of Customer Outputs to Redwood.

Feedback and Model Training. Redwood may collect aggregated and de-identified usage data and feedback (\"Feedback Data\") to improve the performance, accuracy and reliability of the Service. Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train foundational models or to create model weights for sale or redistribution without Customer's prior written consent. Customers may opt-out of Feedback Data collection for model improvement by selecting the relevant option in the Order Form. Feedback Data does not include content that reasonably could contain PHI as defined by applicable law; such content will not be used for training and will be handled in accordance with the Agreement's Data Protection provisions."

Operational notes: anonymization pipeline (30-day retention), logs retention (30 days by default, extendable by request), support for a per-deal opt-out flag.

If Rishi or Laura see a revenue or SLA implication, flag it and I can adjust.

-Aditya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Alex / Sofia / Procurement —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed Order Form redline (CYH_Proposed_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx) and a short feedback license text. High level: we accept that CypherHealth will retain title to Customer Outputs; in return Redwood asks for the limited rights described by Aditya so we can operate and improve the service.

Two options for you to consider (pick one in the Order Form):
1) Standard — allow Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified Feedback Data for model quality improvements; 30-day retention for raw examples; opt-out available.
2) No-Training — allow Redwood operational logs and aggregated telemetry for billing/SLA; expressly prohibit any use of Customer Data or Customer Outputs for model training without written consent.

If you select No-Training, there's a small change in pricing and SLAs (see paragraph 7 of the redline, which notes: additional engineering effort and storage for segregated opt-out flows). I flagged a nominal fee and slightly longer incident response SLA (from 4 hours to 8 hours) to reflect that.

Next step: if the proposal looks acceptable, procurement can confirm the option and we'll route to DocuSign. If you'd like legal-to-legal redlines, Aditya is available for a 30-min call tomorrow.

—Monica
